title: Week of Aug 24–30
subtitle: Block 3, Big-4 retest — Week 2 (first push week). Calibration is banked; now the bar moves. Ride Wednesday, ≥17 running miles, and the volume floor is back on every lift day.
goals: The volume question, answered with the log: last week you did ~48 working sets and ~26k lb — Block 1's calibration week was 65 sets and ~37k lb, and its build weeks ran 86–87 sets and 45–48k. So yes, you were down about 30%, and your journals called it correctly (2-set accessories, thin core). This week is rebuilt to ~73 planned sets: back-off sets on the main lifts, 3-set accessories everywhere, a superset every lift day, and 6+ core sets every lift day. The only volume you're 'missing' vs Block 1 is the fourth barbell day — and that slot is deliberately your 25–30 mile ride.

Push week targets, straight off calibration: Squat 195×5 (was 185, felt easy — Block 1 best is 200×5, week 3 takes it), Bench 180×5 (was 175×5 solid, best 190), Strict OHP 110×5 (you beat the 100 placeholder with 105s), Deadlift 265×4 (was 255×4, best 275). Top sets at ~2 RIR, unspotted bench rules as always, full back protocol on every hinge.

Aerobic reality check: you're not in the worst shape of your life, you're three weeks past a road trip, a bridge week, and a calibration week at 15 miles — and your easy runs have been drifting to ~152 avg HR, which is Z3 pretending to be easy. Detraining plus junk-easy pace is exactly what 'kicked my butt' intervals feel like. The fix is boring: this week holds ~17.5 running miles where easy actually means ≤150, one controlled threshold session Tuesday, and Wednesday's ride as a 2-hour aerobic base session. Strength stays the block's focus — this is the not-atrophying floor, and Block 4 (Sep 14) is where mileage builds for real.

Wednesday is the ride: 25–30 miles, steady Z2 spin, eat before and during. It replaces the Wednesday barbell slot this week, and it's logged under its own distance field so it doesn't inflate the run-mileage stat. Thursday's upper session slides in behind it — arms don't care about bike miles.

Core, rotated per the new floor: Mon = hollow hold / bird dog / suitcase carry, Thu = ab wheel / Pallof / woodchopper, Sat (deadlift day, spine-friendly) = side plank / dead bug / hanging leg raise. Six sets minimum each day, run as 20s-transition circuits. Friday's mini-pump adds 4 more.
Food: maintenance, deficit 0, band 189–191 with the waist as arbiter. You're fueling PR attempts and a 2-hour ride this week — under-eating is the one way to lose both.

Progress tab note: the daily lifting volume chart is gone — it mostly showed which days you lift. In its place is an 8-week lifting volume graph, so the exact drop we just diagnosed is visible on one screen from now on.
review: Calibration week delivered everything it needed to despite starting on an engagement weekend: Squat 185×5 easy, Bench 175×5, strict OHP 105×5 past its placeholder, Deadlift 255×4, and honest journals that reshaped this plan — the 6-set core floor and the third accessory set are your notes, now standing rules. Two honest readings to hold lightly: the pull-up benchmark at 14 (Block 2 exit was 18 — but that one came fresh on a calisthenics day; this one came the morning after a full upper session, so the trend is muddier than the number) and Thursday's intervals feeling terrible (day-after-squat legs, first outdoor speed in a month, and easy runs that have been creeping hot). Saturday's 26-mile ride with Morgan was the best kind of unplanned — legs sore, aerobic system fed. Week 2's job: move every bar 5–10 lb, put the set volume back, and make easy mean easy.

days.name: Quality Run — Controlled Threshold
warmup: 2×20s relaxed strides before the first rep

run.title: Cruise Intervals — 5.5 mi total
run.detail: 1.5 mi easy warm-up → 3 × 6 min at threshold effort (comfortably hard — short sentences, not gasps) with 2 min easy jog between → easy cool-down to round out 5.5. Last week's session kicked your butt because of day-after-squat legs and a month off speed — same legs situation today, so the assignment is CONTROL: start the first rep slower than feels right and finish each rep feeling like you could do one more. If rep 1 blows past comfortably hard, cut reps to 5 min and call it a full success. The paper will look mediocre for a few more weeks. That's detraining unwinding, not your ceiling.

days.name: Ride — 25–30 mi Aerobic Base
days.desc: The centerpiece of the anti-atrophy plan: 25–30 miles at a steady Z2 spin — conversational the whole way, gears you can turn smoothly, HR ideally under ~145. Two hours of pure aerobic base with zero pounding, the day before an upper (not lower) lift by design. Eat a real breakfast, bring fuel for anything past 90 minutes, and drink more than feels necessary. Saturday's ride with Morgan was 26 miles — same neighborhood of effort, just keep this one honest Z2 rather than social-surge pace. Logged under its own distance field so run mileage stays clean.

run.detail: The week's longest run, and the one that rebuilds the aerobic base — IF it stays easy. Your recent 'easy' runs have averaged ~152, which is the no-man's-land that makes everything feel worse. Cap it at 150, and if that means 10:30 miles right now, run 10:30 miles; the pace comes back to the HR within weeks, that's the whole trick. Deadlifts tomorrow — finish feeling like you did nothing.
